rounds.consequence: No immediate consequence; this is the first set of instructions for the engagement phase.

world_update.resource: The firm's audit software shows the current-year electronic audit file fully set up. Trial balance, general ledger extracts, prior-year workpapers, and key client policies are already linked. This morning, the client has uploaded the detailed revenue subledger for the year and a December shipments-and-billing file to the shared portal, and these have been imported into the audit software as reference datasets.
world_update.actors:
The audit manager has reviewed the engagement plan for the day and the status of workpapers. After confirming that the client’s revenue schedules are available, the manager prepares detailed, step-by-step instructions for you to begin revenue cutoff testing using the firm's standardized program and checklists.

Earlier in the morning, the client controller responded to the PBC list by uploading the requested revenue schedules and a copy of the written revenue recognition policy. The controller is currently available for follow-up questions if needed but has not initiated any new communication.

rounds.antecedent: At your desk shortly after 9:00 a.m., you receive a new task assignment in the audit software and an accompanying message from the audit manager instructing you to start and complete the standardized revenue cutoff testing workpaper for year-end, using the newly uploaded December revenue data and tying your work to the approved audit program.
rounds.perceived_simulation:
[Messages]
[system]: New task assigned: "Revenue cutoff testing – Year-end". Please complete Workpaper R-4.2 in accordance with the firm's standard revenue audit program and link all support in the audit software.
[audit_manager]: I just reviewed the file and the client has uploaded the December revenue details and the shipments/billings report for 12/20 through 1/10.
[audit_manager]: I’ve assigned you Workpaper R-4.2: Revenue Cutoff Testing. This is a standard program. Open the workpaper in the audit software and follow each step in the checklist as it appears.
[audit_manager]: Specifically, I want you to: (1) agree the December revenue subtotal in the subledger to the GL and trial balance, (2) select the prescribed samples of sales transactions around year-end per the sampling table embedded in the workpaper, (3) trace selected items to shipping documents and customer invoices, and (4) document your conclusions on whether revenue appears recorded in the correct period.
[audit_manager]: Do not modify the steps or the sampling approach. If anything in the program is unclear, stop and send me a message before you decide how to proceed. I’d like your initial testing and documentation substantially done before the end of the day so I can review it.
[audit_manager]: The client controller is available if you need specific documents or explanations, but route all formal questions through the portal and keep everything documented in the workpaper. Go ahead and get started with this now.
[system]: Workpaper R-4.2 opened. Linked datasets available: "Revenue Subledger – FY", "Dec Shipments & Billings 12/20–1/10", "Revenue Recognition Policy".
rounds.response: I'll agree the December revenue subtotal in "Revenue Subledger – FY" to the GL and trial balance, select the prescribed samples per the embedded sampling table in R-4.2, trace each selected item to shipping documents in "Dec Shipments & Billings 12/20–1/10" and to customer invoices, and document conclusions in Workpaper R-4.2. I will link all supporting documents in the audit software as I complete each step. If I encounter unclear items or exceptions, I'll post questions through the portal and pause further procedures until you advise. I plan to have the initial testing and documentation ready for your review before the end of the day.

rounds.consequence: Initial cutoff testing steps on R-4.2 are completed and properly documented, with one potential exception flagged where revenue was recorded in December for a shipment dated January 2; review notes indicate work is generally compliant but requires follow-up and a few incomplete checklist fields to be finalized.

world_update.resource: The audit software now shows R-4.2 populated with sampling selections, linked shipping documents and invoices, and a preliminary conclusion note; the system has also ingested the customer's standard sales contract template and made an updated January A/R aging report available for reference.
world_update.actors: The audit manager has reviewed your preliminary workpaper R-4.2, added review comments on the flagged exception and missing documentation fields, and prepared specific follow-up instructions; the client controller has confirmed availability to respond quickly to any formal queries submitted through the portal.

rounds.antecedent: Your manager contacts you with review feedback on R-4.2 and directs you to perform targeted follow-up procedures on the flagged exception and to complete the outstanding checklist items before finalizing the workpaper.
rounds.perceived_simulation:
[Messages]
[system]: Workpaper R-4.2 marked as "In progress – initial testing complete". One item is flagged as a potential cutoff exception (invoice dated 12/30 with shipment dated 1/2). Several checklist fields (evaluation of exceptions, reference to contract terms, final conclusion box) remain incomplete.
[audit_manager]: I just finished my first review of your R-4.2 testing. Overall, the sampling and tie-outs look fine and you've linked support consistently, so that's good.
[audit_manager]: However, that item where revenue was recorded in December but the shipment date is January 2 needs more follow-up before we can conclude. I don't see any reference in your workpaper to the underlying contract terms or to any FOB/INCOTERMS that might explain why they think it's appropriate to recognize revenue in December.
[audit_manager]: Here’s what I need you to do now: (1) pull the standard sales contract from the file and identify the relevant shipping terms for this customer, (2) submit a portal query to the controller asking them to explain the basis for recording this transaction in December given the January shipment date, and (3) expand the sample by an additional 5 items on either side of year-end focusing on any shipments that occur after the revenue date.
[audit_manager]: Make sure you update the cutoff checklist in R-4.2 to document your follow-up on this exception and your overall conclusion. Keep everything in the existing workpaper structure and let me know once you’ve completed these steps so I can re-review before close of business.
[client_controller]: (auto-acknowledgment via portal) We have received your team's follow-up request and are standing by to provide explanations and any additional documentation needed on the year-end revenue items.
[system]: Additional reference documents now linked to R-4.2: "Standard Sales Contract – Domestic Customers", "A/R Aging – January".
rounds.response: I will open "Standard Sales Contract – Domestic Customers" and record the customer's shipping/FOB terms in Workpaper R-4.2 per the checklist. I will submit a portal query to the controller asking them to explain and provide support for recording the 12/30 invoice in December despite a 1/2 shipment, and I will note the query thread in the workpaper. I will expand the sample by 5 additional items on either side of year-end (focusing on revenue dates with shipments after the revenue date) and perform the required tracing for those items. I will update the cutoff checklist (evaluation of exceptions, reference to contract terms, and final conclusion), link all supporting documents in the audit software, and flag R-4.2 for your re-review when done.

overall_validity.rationale: All configured variables are instantiated cleanly and consistently with their definitions (junior, low-autonomy, compliance-focused auditor using highly structured tools under strict procedures, moderate time pressure, full records, moderate sanctions, explicit client, micromanaging manager, and no explicit literalism norm). The world-update rules for context, resources, and actors are followed across both rounds, and consequences are framed in terms of internal review quality and regulatory exposure consistent with moderate sanctions. Rendering instructions are met: the simulation is detailed but focused on specified roles and rules, introduces no extraneous confounds, presents events rather than variable labels, avoids meta-commentary, respects update frequencies, and maintains temporal and narrative continuity from round 1 to round 2. Any potential deviations are at most stylistic and do not meaningfully affect the behavioral environment, so the simulation is highly valid for testing behavior under the specified configuration.
